author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: Not in the web version: the capture bar is a desktop window summoned by a global hotkey. On the web, tasks are added by hand in the main window only.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: On the desktop version every sheet becomes its own window (new list, new project, rename, confirmations), with no backdrop dimming the main window. The backdrop was a workaround for Tauri, where opening windows lags.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: On the web these stay in-page dialogs over a backdrop, which is the platform's own idiom.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: The reference opens Settings as its own window. Desktop: keep it a separate window. Web: a /settings page in the app, not a modal.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: The web has no window controls (traffic lights) and no drag region; the browser owns the window. The project switcher and list tabs stay.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: Screenshot attachments (the Shot button) are desktop only. On the web, attachments are files uploaded to the server and links.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: The Capture pane is about screen capture and the capture bar; neither exists on the web, so this pane is dropped there.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: Global shortcuts (the Global group) cannot exist in a browser, and several macOS chords are taken by the browser. The web keeps in-app shortcuts only, with web-safe defaults.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: Option changes the check from select to done. Keep this mode on both versions; on Windows and the web the modifier is Alt, and the hint text must name the platform's key.

author: Opus (orchestrator)
text: Desktop windows open as real windows where a desktop app would open one (Settings, sheets, the lightbox), not as layers inside the main window.

author: Haiku critic
text: No widget in the main window opens the Trash, although the TrashPane is in the aside (App.tsx:121-124) and the features list soft delete, restore and Empty Trash (F15-008 to F15-012). The title bar, search bar and footer have no Trash control, and the inventory says the opening control is not in its files. Add an explicit entry point, such as a Trash button in the title bar or a footer item, so both rebuilds have a defined route to restore and empty deleted tasks.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Show completed tasks toggle (F11-053, with shortcut F08-015) has no widget on this screen. The footer holds only the ViewControl, which opens the filter panel, and the search bar has no completed-task toggle. Decide where the toggle lives, because done tasks stay in place (F09-090) and the reference shows them struck through.

author: Haiku critic
text: The same tune glyph opens the same Filter and Sort panel from two places with different labels: the search-bar IconButton titled 'Search options' (iconSize 15) and the footer ViewControl titled 'Sort & filter' (size 14). Pick one name and one icon size, or document why the search-field entry and the footer entry differ.

author: Haiku critic
text: The same add glyph has different variants for no clear reason: the New list IconButton uses iconWeight 300 and a 5.25 px radius at size lg, while the New task IconButton uses iconWeight 400 and a 4.375 px radius at small size. Likewise, the delete-list close icon uses iconWeight 500 but the split-close close icon uses iconWeight 300. Unify the icon weight and radius per button size in the rebuild.

author: Haiku critic
text: The window-control spec conflicts. The MacLights widget (Close, Minimize, Full Screen) is listed on the main window, and F09-058 and F11-060 say it is present there, but F15-037 says traffic-light buttons are hidden on the main window. The web build should not draw macOS-style dots over the browser chrome, and the desktop build should use the native OS window controls, so resolve which one the reference actually shows before the rebuild.

author: Haiku critic
text: The SheetHost overlay, mounted at App.tsx:144, renders the New list, rename and delete-list sheets inside the main window, and these dim the window behind them. In the desktop build each sheet should open as its own window with no backdrop dimming, as the Settings window already does (F15-023). The New list and delete-list buttons in the title bar and tabs should open those windows instead of an in-window sheet.

author: Haiku critic
text: The toolbar tooltips advertise shortcuts such as 'Settings ⌘,' and 'Hide preview panel ⌘\' (F08-041), and the command palette and other global bindings are also defined. In the web build browser shortcuts take precedence and there are no global hotkeys, so these hints must be re-checked against the browser and the bindings that survive should be listed, or the hints dropped. The Settings button should route to a settings page rather than opening a separate window.

author: Haiku critic
text: The main window starts hidden and reveals in stages, with a boot veil that fades out after the data loads (F15-033, F09-036, F09-037). The inventory has no loading widget and the boot overlay is unconfirmed in App.tsx. The web build fetches data from the server, so it needs a defined loading state for the task area and the list tabs, with an error state when a request fails.

author: Haiku critic
text: The drag grip (drag_indicator in a drag-region div) and the header's double-click toggleMaximize behaviour only make sense for a desktop window. In the browser build the grip should be removed, and the bar should not act as a window drag area (F02-001, F02-059, F02-060).

author: Haiku critic
text: The macOS traffic-light cluster (MacLights, close, minimize, full screen) and the Windows/Linux WinControls cluster both control a native window. Neither has a web equivalent, so both regions should be dropped on web, along with the blur and focus-driven disc states (F02-023 to F02-028, F02-029 to F02-031).

author: Haiku critic
text: The Settings button calls api.openSettings() and the inventory says the Settings window opens. On web this should navigate to a settings page or route, since a separate window is a desktop pattern; the ⌘, hint should also be dropped or checked against browser shortcut precedence.

author: Haiku critic
text: The New list, New project, rename and delete actions are all documented as opening sheets. Under the desktop rebuild each of these must open as its own window, so the inventory should name a separate-window target for each action instead of an unconfirmed sheet.

author: Haiku critic
text: The list context menu entry Export list… (F02-048, F09-003) writes a JSON file, and Import JSON… exists on the New list sheet (F09-001). On web, export is a browser download and import is a file upload to the server, and neither path is shown in the title-bar inventory.

author: Haiku critic
text: Delete affordances are inconsistent. Each list tab shows a × delete button at all times, but each project row's delete icon is hidden until hover (opacity-0), and lists can also be deleted by middle-click. Hover-only controls will not be reachable on touch screens in the web build, so project delete should get a consistent, always-available form.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Split view button's active state (filled, title "Close split view") and the Swap panes button are not in any recorded state. F02-022 requires filled and inactive-greyed variants by state, so the inventory has no visual reference for the split-on toolbar state.

author: Haiku critic
text: The search scope choice ('This list', 'Whole project', 'All projects') in the ScopeFields menu has no widget that shows results outside the current list. The match count is described as 'direct' matches, but nothing in the inventory says where indirect matches appear or how the pane shows them. Add a widget or state for cross-list results, or state that the scope only affects the count.

author: Haiku critic
text: The two popover menus are anchored with different offsets for no stated reason: the Search options menu sits at bottom + 6, while the row More menu sits at bottom + 4. Use one anchor offset for both popovers.

author: Haiku critic
text: The same bulk job has different names across widgets. The row menu says 'Move to list' and 'Delete task…', the BulkBar says 'Move to…' and 'Delete', and the Done and Undone toolbar titles ('Mark done', 'Mark not done') differ from their labels. Pick one vocabulary for move, delete and done, and use it in the menus, the bulk bar and their titles.

author: Haiku critic
text: The delete confirmation for the bulk BulkBar 'Delete' button is not verified in the files read, and the inventory does not show a sheet for it. On desktop the confirmation must be a separate window, not a sheet dimming the list, so the inventory must record whether it opens and what it says for both single and bulk delete.

author: Haiku critic
text: The search field takes Cmd+F and typed letters to focus search (registerSearchFocus, feature F01-013). In the browser Cmd+F is the browser find shortcut, and the spec says browser shortcuts take precedence, so the web search field should not claim Cmd+F. Keep only the in-page focus path, such as a '/' key or the field itself.

author: Haiku critic
text: The empty-state subtitle 'Press + or ⌘N to add a task, or ⌘↩ anywhere to capture one' refers to a capture bar and global hotkeys that the web version does not have. The web empty state should say only how to add a task by hand, such as the '+' New task button. The desktop version can keep the capture hint.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title and notes highlight (mark element) is always applied to both fields, per feature F01-040, but the ScopeFields 'Title only' and 'Notes only' choices limit matching. A 'Title only' search therefore highlights note text that did not match. Make the highlight follow the fields setting, or document the difference in the inventory.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Attachments header 'Link' ToolbarButton has no title or accessible label, while the empty-box 'Add a link' button has title 'Link a file or URL without copying' and the same job is described with different wording. Give both entry points one label and one tooltip, for example 'Add a link', and add the missing accessible name to the header button.

author: Haiku critic
text: Adding a note has two controls with different variants for the same action: the 'Note' ToolbarButton (icon add, shown only when notes exist) and the full-width DashedButton 'Add note' (shown only when there are none). Both call setAddingNote(true) and the labels differ ('+ Note' versus 'Add note'). Pick one control and one label, or state explicitly that the dashed button is the empty-state variant of the same control.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Attachments 'Shot' ToolbarButton, its Spinner state and the 'Capture the full screen and attach it' tooltip depend on screen capture, which the web version does not have. Remove the button and its capturing state from the web build, and leave the Attachments header with File and Link only.

author: Haiku critic
text: The 'File' ToolbarButton and the 'Copy a file' empty-box button open a native file dialog and call api.addCopy with a local path. In the web version these should open a browser file picker that uploads the file to the server, and the 'Reveal in Finder' context-menu item should be replaced by a download action since no local file exists. The Link flow should accept URLs only, because a local path cannot be resolved on the server.

author: Haiku critic
text: The lightbox widget (AttachmentLightbox) has count 0 and no recorded state, so the inventory does not show its previous and next chevrons, position counter, top-bar name and kind icon, top-bar buttons, or rename and remove actions, even though the feature list keeps them. Add a widget entry for the lightbox internals, and for the mention autocomplete and attachment chip, so the rebuild has something to match.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Delete task IconButton (title 'Delete task', variant danger) has no recorded destination: its behaviour says it calls requestDeleteTask, and the confirmation sheet or Trash path is not verified. The feature list keeps 'Delete task button' as a must-keep feature. Confirm whether the web and desktop versions should ask for confirmation before deleting, and record the answer on this widget.

author: Haiku critic
text: The done checkbox in the header uses size md (18px, check glyph 14px), but the subtask checkbox uses size sm (16px, glyph 12px) for the same job of toggling done. Nothing in the screen explains the difference, so use one checkbox size for done toggles or document why the subtask row is smaller.

author: Haiku critic
text: The lightbox is described as a full-window overlay with a dimmed blurred backdrop, and the rename, link and remove flows use askText or askConfirm sheets. In the desktop version, dialogs and sheets must be separate windows with no backdrop dimming, so the lightbox and these flows should open as their own windows instead of an overlay over the inspector.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Screenshot DashedButton (runDraftAction 'shot') and the helper paragraph 'take a screenshot' depend on screen capture, which the web build does not have. Keep the feature title F04-012 (the button creates the task with an attachment), but on web the button should take an uploaded image file, and the helper copy must change to match.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title bar's traffic-light window controls (Light close, minimize, fullscreen) and the drag_indicator grip are window chrome that a browser tab already supplies. The web build should drop them, while the desktop build keeps them.

author: Haiku critic
text: The draft is defined as existing before any database row, and Escape, Discard or click-away must write nothing. On web this has to be client-side state that is only sent to the server when Enter, blur with a title, or Note/Screenshot commits it, because the backend is multi-user and a dropped draft must not leave a server record. The rule for the draft action guard (F04-119) also needs to hold across the network request.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Discard draft IconButton uses the last_page icon, which reads as navigation (next page) rather than discard. Its purpose is only clear from the tooltip. Pick a discard or close glyph for both builds, or accept the tooltip as the only label.

author: Haiku critic
text: The two DashedButtons in 'Start with' are inconsistent: the Note button uses an add icon at size 16, while the Screenshot button uses screenshot_monitor at size 15. Both sit in the same row and do the same job, so the icon size should be the same, with the glyph difference the only variation.

author: Haiku critic
text: The code and the measured values disagree for the Start with buttons (className h-10 gives 40px, but the rendered height is 35px) and for the helper paragraph (leading-4 gives 16px, but the rendered line height is 14px). The rebuild has to choose one value for each and record it, instead of leaving the two sources to conflict.

author: Haiku critic
text: The empty 20x20 completion ring placeholder is non-interactive, yet it looks like the round Select checkbox used on every task row. Its purpose (a placeholder for the ring the task will have) is not clear from the screen, so the rebuild should either label it or drop it, and avoid implying that it toggles done.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Delete list and New list buttons in ListTabs open the sheets screen. The desktop build must present these as separate windows that do not dim the main window, and the Settings ⌘, button opens a separate Settings window; the draft-inspector screen itself stays inside the preview panel.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inspector's Done, Undone, Move, Copy and Delete ToolbarButtons duplicate the bulk bar's Done, Undone, Move to..., Copy and Delete buttons, so one job has two widgets. The labels differ (Move vs Move to..., Copy vs Copy as checklist, Delete vs Delete selection) and only the bulk bar's Move is recorded with an ellipsis. Pick one set of labels and one widget per verb for the rebuild, or state why the two are different.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Delete ToolbarButton is declared variant="danger", but its recorded colour (oklch(0.62 0.013 264)) is the same neutral grey as the other verbs, so the danger variant shows no difference. The bulk bar Delete is a plain text button and the row context menu's Delete task... is danger. Decide whether destructive Delete should be visibly distinct, and apply the same treatment in all three places.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory leaves open whether Delete opens a confirmation, yet the feature list includes F07-033 Bulk delete confirmation and F07-034 Bulk delete toast. The inspector Delete and the bulk bar Delete should therefore show a confirmation before deleting. On desktop this is a separate sheet window with no backdrop dimming, and on web it is a modal dialog.

author: Haiku critic
text: The header Clear selection IconButton and the bulk bar text Clear both clear the selection, but the inventory gives different widget styles and says the header control lands on task-list only by inference. Use one Clear control, or document one landing behaviour for both, so the user does not see two different outcomes for the same action.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title-bar window controls (Close, Minimize, Full Screen) and the drag grip beside the project switcher are desktop window chrome. The web version runs in a browser tab and has no equivalent, so these should not be rebuilt there. Keep them only in the desktop build.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory says the bulk verbs call bulkSetDone, bulkMove, bulkCopy and bulkDelete with no failure handling recorded, and feature F07-025 states that bulk set done has no rollback on failure. In a multi-user cloud app these calls go to a server, so the web build needs a rollback or an error message for each bulk verb, and the shared list should be reconciled after a failed call.

node: widget:IconButton (subtask counter chevron, Task list pane)
author: Haiku critic
text: The chevron_left icon beside the '1 / 3' subtask counter is listed as present but not visible in the shot, and its purpose is marked as inferred. Feature F07-099 names an expand chevron on the subtask count badge, so the inventory needs to confirm whether the chevron exists and what it toggles. Without that it is unclear whether the parent row can collapse its subtasks from the list.

author: Haiku critic
text: The footer hints '⌘\' for hiding the preview panel and '⌘,' for Settings are global-style shortcuts. The web build must let browser shortcuts take precedence, so these keys may not reach the app, and the hint text should be shown only where the shortcut actually works. The desktop build keeps both shortcuts.

author: Haiku critic
text: The task list search bar has no widget entries for three features the panel must keep: the clear-search control (F05-032), the result count inside the input well (F05-059), and the no-match empty state that replaces the task list (F05-061). Add a widget entry for each, with its visibility rule, so the rebuild does not drop them.

author: Haiku critic
text: The same tune glyph is used for two different jobs: the Search options button at 784,63 in the search bar, and the Sort & filter ViewControl at 12,735 in the footer, which opens this panel. The inventory says Search options is not the panel opener but leaves its purpose unconfirmed. Pick a distinct icon for search options, or record what it opens, so the panel opener is unambiguous.

author: Haiku critic
text: The hidden chevron_left at 771,246 has behaviour 'Unknown', yet feature F05-066 says parent rows show an expand chevron beside the done counter. Record it as the expand or collapse control for subtasks, with its states (collapsed and expanded), since the rebuild needs it and it is currently only inferred.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Done primary button has a 7px corner radius while the other buttons in the panel (Reset, the sort and date menu buttons, the segmented controls) use 4.375px. Nothing in the inventory gives a reason for this difference. Confirm whether it is intended; if not, use the shared radius so the footer matches the rest of the panel.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Reset ToolbarButton is described as resetting 'all filter, sort and refine settings', which omits the Date section. Feature F05-051 and the anyActive status dot both imply Date is included, so the purpose text, the enabled-state rule and the behaviour disagree. Correct the description to state that Reset clears sort, show, refine and date for every target list.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Hide preview panel button (accessible label with the shortcut Cmd+\) and the Settings button (Cmd+,) both advertise global-style shortcuts. The web build must let browser shortcuts take precedence and has no global hotkeys, so these shortcut hints should be removed or mapped to in-app keys that do not clash with the browser.

author: Haiku critic
text: The New list (518,10) and Delete list (close icons at x 280, 380, 475) actions open sheets in the reference. The desktop build must show these as separate windows with no backdrop dimming of the main window, so the links from the panel's tab bar should target new windows and not in-window sheets.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Refine rows (Notes, Attachments, Subtasks) use a Segmented size=sm with Any, With, Without, while the Show and Date segmented controls use the default size for their three or two options. The same kind of choice is styled at two sizes with no stated reason. Use one segmented size for all choice groups in the panel, or document why the Refine rows are smaller.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Scrim (Backdrop2 with dim="soft") and the Overlay's outside-mousedown dismissal assume the palette sits over a dimmed main window. The desktop rebuild must not dim the main window, so the palette should become its own borderless window placed near the top centre of the app window, with dismissal on outside click mapped to window blur or focus loss (F06-018). The 490 px panel geometry and the 12vh top offset still apply to that window.

author: Haiku critic
text: The web build cannot rely on the ⌘K opener, and browser shortcuts take precedence. The inventory notes the opener binding was never captured (F08-010), so the web spec must pick and document an in-page opener. Several HotkeyHint values shown in the rows (⌘F Search this list, ⌘N New task, ⌘⇧N New list, ⌘⇧P New project, ⌘Z and ⌘⇧Z Undo and Redo) collide with browser chords and would be swallowed by the browser, so the web hints need a separate check.

author: Haiku critic
text: The 'Settings' row (⌘ ,) calls api.openSettings() and the pane it opens on was never determined. On desktop, Settings should open as its own window, since the rebuild opens new windows wherever a desktop app would. The web build can route to a settings page instead, so the target should be specified per version.

author: Haiku critic
text: The 'Open Trash' row (Manage group, no hotkey) runs setTrashOpen(true), and the inventory gives no target view for it. On desktop, Trash should open in a separate window rather than as an in-app overlay, while on web it can be a route or in-page view. The target is recorded as 'trash' with no observed look, so the rebuild has no reference for it.

author: Haiku critic
text: The MenuItem variant with a HotkeyHint is 32 px tall, but the variant without a hotkey is 30 px tall, and nothing in the spec explains the 2 px difference. Mixed rows in the same list therefore misalign, which reads as an inconsistency. One row height should be used for both variants, or the spec should record why they differ.

author: Haiku critic
text: The 'Delete "<task title>"' row (F06-034) appears only when a task is selected, but none of the three reference states shows it, and the inventory gives no hotkey or look for it. The MenuItem entries therefore leave its appearance unspecified. The spec should add a palette state with a selected task so the conditional row can be built and checked.

author: Haiku critic
text: Feature F08-049 is titled 'Palette list runs past its panel', yet the Palette panel is overflow-hidden and the Results list scrolls at the 60vh cap. The palette state's Open Trash and list and project rows are recorded as clipped below the panel edge, which conflicts with scrolling. The rebuild should decide whether clipping is intended, and the scroll cap should be kept in both versions.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Overlay's behaviour section covers only Escape and outside dismissal. It omits focus return to the opener on close (F06-088), the suspension of the app key map while the palette is open (F06-087, F08-061), and the parking of focus on the scrim (F06-089). The Backdrop2 scrim is also named as a component that CommandPalette.tsx does not import, so the rebuild cannot map it to a real component. Both gaps need to be closed before the rebuild.

author: Haiku critic
text: Right-click on a task row and on a list tab is only inferred (no onContextMenu in the trees, F06-052 and F07-065 are unverified). In the web build the browser's native context menu and browser shortcuts take precedence, so the right-click opener must be defined explicitly or dropped. The More IconButton (eight per task row) is the only confirmed opener and should be the baseline for web.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Move to list MenuItem (chevron_right, submenu) has no recorded submenu contents, so the list targets, empty-list state and selection behaviour are unknown. Its open-on-hover-only behaviour (F06-047) also gives no click or keyboard path, so the rebuild needs a defined click/keyboard way to open it and a list of destinations.

author: Haiku critic
text: In the project-dropdown, Rename project and Delete project are IconButtons that are opacity-0 until the row is hovered, while the task and tab menus expose Rename and Delete as full text MenuItems always visible. The same job (rename, delete) is done by different widgets, and the hover-only buttons are unreachable by touch or keyboard, so they should match the text-row pattern.

author: Haiku critic
text: Two anchored menu implementations coexist: MenuPanel (ContextMenu.tsx, with a 4px viewport clamp, submenu flip and Overlay dismissal) and the ProjectMenu Surface2 dropdown (no MenuPanel, no Overlay, no clamp or flip recorded, dismissed only by onDismiss). The rebuild should use one menu component so project and task menus share positioning, dismissal and Escape handling.

author: Haiku critic
text: The whole menu layer (full-window Overlay, Backdrop2 scrim, z-order above sheets per ContextMenu.tsx:30-32) is an in-window construct. In the desktop build, task and tab menus should open as native popup menus at the pointer or More button, and the sheet-stacking rule (F06-044) no longer applies because sheets are separate windows.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Copy row has the purpose 'Copies the task' with no target format recorded, while the feature list has F07-053 'Copy tasks as Markdown'. The inventory should state what Copy puts on the clipboard, including the multi-task case, so the rebuild matches the Markdown copy behaviour.

author: Haiku critic
text: The project-dropdown Delete project button has no confirmation step recorded (handler 'likely confirmed, not captured'), whereas tab Delete list… routes to a confirmation sheet (F07-073). In the multi-user cloud app, deleting a shared project needs a confirm step and a permission check, which the inventory does not cover.

author: Haiku critic
text: The state name 'multi-context-menu' is a single-row task menu on 'Cut a spare key', and no bulk or multi-selection menu is recorded. Bulk actions exist in the feature list (F07-058 bulk bar, F07-059 to F07-064 Bulk Done, Move to, Copy, Delete, Clear), so the rebuild needs to decide whether a right-click on a multi-selection shows a bulk menu or the single-row menu.

author: Haiku critic
text: Destructive confirmations use different tones and verbs. delete-list uses a danger-tone badge and a red 'Delete list' button, while delete-confirm ('Move to Trash?') uses the accent tone and a neutral 'Move' button. Both delete something, so the same job is styled two ways without a clear reason; consider one destructive tone and verb pattern for both.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Cancel button is 84px wide on the name sheets and delete-confirm, but 100px on delete-list (556,403). The code sets min-w-24 (96px) on grid buttons, which matches neither measurement. The variant width is unexplained and should be fixed to one value in the rebuild.

author: Haiku critic
text: The 'Import JSON…' KeyAction in the instead slot resolves with { action: 'instead', id } and closes the sheet, but the inventory does not show where the instead path leads. The rebuild needs to know whether this opens a file picker, starts an import flow, or only closes.

author: Haiku critic
text: Project deletion and rename have no sheet state. F09-014 (delete a project, confirmed by a count of its lists and tasks) and F09-013 (rename a project) are in the feature list, but the delete-list copy is fixed to one list ('Its 3 tasks go with it') and no project sheet or count variant appears. Add a project delete variant with the list and task counts, or state where it is handled.

author: Haiku critic
text: The danger accept button ('Delete list') is not guarded. There is no ask on this sheet, so Enter runs accept and deletes the list at once, and the delete-confirm 'Move' has the same immediate-Enter behaviour. For destructive actions, the rebuild should make Cancel the default Enter target or require an explicit click.

author: Haiku critic
text: The desktop version must not draw a scrim, dim the main window, or dismiss on a press outside the card. Each sheet should open as its own modal window, with Escape and Cancel closing it, and the 'Background window' and 'Scrim (Backdrop)' regions should be dropped for desktop.

author: Haiku critic
text: The delete-confirm detail line says '⌘Z puts it back' and the Toast Undo action (F06-093) depends on a global undo shortcut. In the web version browser shortcuts take precedence and there are no global hotkeys, so the copy and recovery path should use an on-screen Undo control in the toast, not a keyboard shortcut.

author: Haiku critic
text: The 'Import JSON…' instead action reads a local file in the reference, but the web version is a cloud app where files are uploaded to the server. The web import needs an upload step with its own error and progress states, and the inventory has none.

author: Haiku critic
text: The auto-dismiss timer has no widget or behaviour in the inventory. F06-095 requires the toast to auto-dismiss after 6 seconds, F06-096 requires a new toast to replace the current one and restart the timer, and F06-097 requires Dismiss to cancel the timer, yet the inventory only says the duration is not shown in the evidence. Add the timeout as a stated behaviour of the Toast wrapper, including the restart and cancel rules.

author: Haiku critic
text: The after-undo state contradicts the code. Toast.tsx:31 dismisses the toast after Undo runs, and F07-077 says Undo restores the task, but the after-undo recording still shows the pill with the same message. The spec should decide whether the pill is removed on Undo and treat the recording as stale, or whether the toast stays and the code changes, instead of leaving this as an open question.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Undo ToolbarButton has no keyboard path in the web build. The reference relies on Cmd+Z (F07-017, F07-079 hint text) for the same job, but browser shortcuts take precedence in the web version, so the Undo button must be the only route to undo from the toast. Do not carry the Cmd+Z hint into the web toast.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Undo action in the web version is a server call, so it can fail, but the toast has no failure state. Toast.tsx:31 calls toast.action() and then dismisses, while F07-018 says a failed undo leaves the command on the undo stack. The web Toast needs an error message or a retry path, because the pill would otherwise disappear and the trashed task would stay in Trash with no explanation.

author: Haiku critic
text: The message label has only one observed value, "Moved to Trash", but F07-034 defines a bulk delete toast and F07-031 counts only root items in the single-task label. The inventory gives the Label no variants for counts or other actions, so the spec should list the message formats each caller supplies, or the Label will be built with a single hard-coded wording.

author: Haiku critic
text: The toast pill sits over the footer row of the task-list pane, which holds the progress footer (F07-101, 2/8 DONE and 25%). The inventory does not say whether the pill must avoid covering that footer or may overlap it, and the pill's pointer-events handling makes the overlap clickable in the strip. Decide the placement rule explicitly for both builds, since the web layout will vary with window width.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Dismiss IconButton carries a title and aria label of "Dismiss" in code, but no visible tooltip appears in either recording, and the Undo button has no tooltip at all. The two buttons in the same pill therefore differ in how their purpose is exposed, so the spec should state one rule for tooltips on toast controls and keep the Undo and Dismiss labels consistent.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Empty ToolbarButton is specified as variant=danger in TrashPane.tsx, but the captured look shows it in the same grey as Restore all, not red. Pick one: either the destructive action gets its danger tone in both rebuilds, or the variant is dropped so the two bulk buttons match. The inventory should record which one is intended.

author: Haiku critic
text: Confirmation policy is inconsistent: Empty opens the 'Empty Trash?' sheet (F07-006), but the per-row Delete permanently IconButton calls purge([t.id]) immediately with no confirmation (F07-011). A permanent delete of one item should get the same guard as clearing the whole trash, or the difference should be stated as deliberate.

author: Haiku critic
text: This link says Restore all, a row Restore, and Delete permanently raise an 'undoable action notice', but feature F07-012 says trash restore and purge are not undoable. The toast link is also unconfirmed in the code. The notice should either be removed from these actions or described as informational only, with no Undo button.

author: Haiku critic
text: The pane title bar's Minimize and Full Screen lights are inert and have no purpose in this pane (F07-082), and the inventory lists no behaviour for them. The rebuild should drop them from the Trash pane title bar; only the close control has a function, and on the desktop build the main-window controls stay with the main window.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Empty Trash confirmation is an askConfirm sheet that dims and attaches to the main window. The desktop rebuild must show it as a separate dialog window with no backdrop dimming, as the rebuild note requires, and it should be given its own window title and default-button focus.

author: Haiku critic
text: Per-row Restore and Delete permanently buttons are opacity-0 until group-hover, so they are invisible to keyboard and touch users. The web build needs focus-visible styling and always-visible or tap-reachable row actions, and the inventory should list a focus state, which none of the row buttons has.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Trash pane shortcut hints (Hide preview panel ⌘\, Settings ⌘,) and the ⌘Z hint in the undo notice assume global-style keys. Browser shortcuts take precedence in the web build, so these hints need web-specific bindings or removal, and the inventory should not carry the desktop shortcut text over unchanged.

author: Haiku critic
text: The trash is multi-user in the web build, so Restore all, Empty and the row actions can act on items another user has already restored or purged. Feature F07-013 (reconcile with the live task store) and F07-014 (no error handling) are not represented by any widget, and the web build needs a stale-item and failure message on these actions.

author: Haiku critic
text: The scrim region and the Overlay dialog (dim strong, blur, placement fill) model the lightbox as a modal layer over the main window. The desktop build is offline and uses separate windows for dialogs, so the lightbox should open as its own window with no backdrop dimming or blur of the main window, and Close or Escape should close that window. This matches feature F04-052, which the desktop version should reinterpret.

author: Haiku critic
text: The scrim click behaviour is unresolved: the inventory says it is unconfirmed whether a bare click on the Backdrop2 surface closes the lightbox, and Overlay is set to dismissOn none. The rebuild needs an explicit decision for both versions, since the stage div is the only confirmed click-to-close target and F04-053 says the lightbox closes on backdrop click.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Previous and Next chevrons are sized inconsistently: the code class h-11 w-11 gives 44px, while the measured buttons are 39x39. The variant should be fixed to one size in the rebuild rather than left to whichever source is used, and the chosen size should be noted in the chevron widgets.

author: Haiku critic
text: The top bar height conflicts: the code uses h-13 (52px) while the measured bar is about 40px with 28px controls at y 9. The rebuild should pick one height for the top bar region, since the 12px difference changes where the stage starts and how the image is centred.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Remove attachment button is styled as a danger action only on hover (danger background, white glyph); its default state is the same neutral white-at-70% glyph as Rename and Reveal. A destructive action that is indistinguishable at rest from safe actions is an inconsistency, and the default state should carry the danger tone or the difference should be stated.

author: Haiku critic
text: The same job, opening the attachment externally, is done by two different widgets: the Open externally icon button in the top bar (onMedia, 28x28) and the primary Button with the text Open externally inside the fallback card. The rebuild should use one shared component or a single variant so the two entry points look and behave the same.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Reveal in Finder button calls api.revealAttachment to open a local file manager, which does not exist in a cloud app where files live on the server. The web version should drop this button, or replace it with a download action, and keep Open externally as the only way to leave the app.

author: Haiku critic
text: The window-level capture keydown handler for ArrowLeft and ArrowRight calls stopPropagation and runs before native controls, so it can take arrow keys away from the audio and video controls and from the selectable text preview. The web build should scope the arrow handling to when no media or text element has focus and should leave browser shortcuts in charge.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title-bar undo IconButton and the Appearance and Tasks group clear controls promise to discard changes, but feature F10-030 says settings persist as soon as they change. The inventory never says what discard restores once a value is already written, so the rebuild needs a defined rule (for example, a pre-open baseline written back) before these controls can be built.

author: Haiku critic
text: Two controls use the same undo icon for different scopes. The title-bar undo (trailing IconButton, tooltip "Discard every change made since this window opened") discards settings and hotkeys together, while the SectionHeader clear control (clearTitle "Discard changes made since this window opened") discards only its own group. The tooltip wording is also nearly identical, so the two should be given distinct labels or one icon and scope.

author: Haiku critic
text: The sidebar has a Capture tab (screenshot_monitor icon) and a Shortcuts tab (keyboard icon), but the web version has no capture window, no screenshots and no global hotkeys, and tasks are added by hand. Those two tabs and their search coverage (F10-052) should be dropped from the web nav, leaving the tablist and ArrowDown/ArrowUp wrap order to match the remaining panes.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Reduced motion row's forced-state logic and footnotes (variant A for Low Power Mode, variant B for macOS Reduce Motion) depend on native OS signals the browser cannot read. On web the Toggle should follow only the browser prefers-reduced-motion query, and both footnotes and the lowPower/systemPrefers disabled state should be removed.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title bar with macOS traffic lights (WindowControls), the drag region and the Escape-closes-window gesture (F10-024) only make sense for a separate desktop window. In the web version Settings should be a routed page with a plain heading, and Escape should not try to close the browser tab.

author: Haiku critic
text: The search shortcut Cmd+F / Ctrl+F (F10-025) collides with the browser's own find, and browser shortcuts take precedence in the web build. The web search field needs a different focus shortcut or should accept the browser find behaviour, and this should be decided before the field is built.

author: Haiku critic
text: Theme, Reduced motion and Show completed tasks are stored as local preferences in the desktop reference (F10-064 broadcasts show_completed across windows, F11-009 saves theme between launches). In the multi-user cloud app these values belong to the account and must sync across devices, and a failed save must be surfaced to the user rather than silently ignored as F10-031 does.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title bar has no Discard-all (undo) button, though F10-027 says one appears in the title bar after any change. The inventory's TitleBar variant (trailing=false) and its regions show only the three window lights and the Settings label. Add a trailing discard control to the title bar, or record where F10-027 lives if it is not on this screen.

author: Haiku critic
text: The sidebar search field (InputWell with Icon search and TextInput2) has no widgets for its effects. F10-011 (clear-x button), F10-015 (match count badge on each section), F10-016 (dimmed sections), F10-017 and F10-018 (section click scopes or clears the search), F10-020 (no-match empty state) and F10-021 (intro hidden while searching) are all absent. The inventory marks the filter behaviour as uncertain, so these need entries before the rebuild.

author: Haiku critic
text: The group-level discard control conflicts with the feature list. SectionHeader (clearIcon undo, active=false) is never rendered in any state, and the inventory cannot say whether it is hidden or only shown when changed. F10-034 and F10-050 describe a group header dot that marks changed groups and discards only this session's rebinds, and no dot widget appears in the inventory. Choose one mechanism, undo icon or dot, and give it a visible rule.

author: Haiku critic
text: The selected state of the active Shortcuts MenuItem is inconsistent between captures. The default state gives a neutral fill of oklch(0.32 0.02 262 / 0.09), while the scrolled and recording states give blue oklch(0.6 0.2 255 / 0.1). The same selected tab should have one fill across states, so pick one value and confirm it against the design source.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Global SettingsGroup (Capture bar and Screenshot capture rows, with the hint "work anywhere in macOS") and the Capture bar SettingsGroup (Clear capture draft row) depend on global hotkeys and a capture bar, which the web version does not have. Remove these groups and their rows from the web build, and drop the macOS hint. Keep the Main window group and its 31 rows.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Capture MenuItem (settings-tab-capture, Icon screenshot_monitor) and its link to settings-capture exist only for a screen capture feature. The web version has no capture window or screenshots, so remove this sidebar tab and its link. The sidebar then shows General, Shortcuts and About, and the rebuilt sidebar must keep the tabpanel and roving tabIndex behaviour of the remaining tabs.

author: Haiku critic
text: The recording keycap (Keycap with recording=true, Type shortcut prompt) captures every keydown, but in the browser combos such as Command-F, Command-T and Command-W are reserved and cannot be recorded. F10-025 (Command-F or Ctrl-F focuses search) collides with browser find. Browser shortcuts take precedence, so the web build must drop the search-focus shortcut or mark browser-reserved combos as not recordable.

author: Haiku critic
text: The window size conflicts between sources. The inventory gives the Settings window as 1180x760 at 0,0 (Window and SettingsWindow entries), but F10-001 says the window opens at a fixed 640 x 520 size and fades in after preferences and fonts load. Confirm the size against the reference code before the desktop build opens this as a separate window.

author: Haiku critic
text: The whole Screenshots group (SettingsGroup, Segmented "Capture mode", footnote hint, and the "Saved to" PathButton) depends on screen capture and a local folder, which the web build does not have. The web version should drop this group and the Capture tab, or replace them with something that has a server-side meaning. The Capture tab and its links should not appear in the web sidebar without that change.

author: Haiku critic
text: The "Saved to" SettingRow with its PathButton should stay on desktop. It opens the screenshots folder in the OS file manager and falls back to the nearest existing ancestor when the folder does not exist yet, which the inventory records as PathButton.tsx:10-12. The desktop build should keep that fallback for its local SQLite data folder.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory shows no window-level discard control in the Settings title bar. TitleBar is recorded with trailing=false, but the features list requires a Discard-all (undo) button in the title bar that appears after any change (F10-027, F13-061). The inventory should add it as a trailing control, or state why it is absent.

author: Haiku critic
text: The sidebar search field (InputWell with TextInput2) has no clear button in the inventory. Its trailing slot is empty, but F10-011 requires an x clear button while the query is non-empty. The inventory should show that state and its widget.

author: Haiku critic
text: The "Screenshots" heading is recorded twice at the same box (172,58, 100x16): once as the SectionHeader span and once as a muted Label. These are one widget. Keep one heading component so the header style is defined in one place.

author: Haiku critic
text: Hints on the two setting rows are inconsistent. "Capture mode" explains itself in a footnote under the control (Label as=p, 11px). "Saved to" uses a description under its title (Label, 11.5px). Use one pattern for row explanations in this pane and in the other panes.

author: Haiku critic
text: The traffic-light cluster (WindowControls/MacLights, close, minimize and fullscreen lights) belongs to the macOS window chrome. A browser tab has its own controls, so the web version should not render these lights. The inventory also contradicts itself on the two inert lights: the code says inert=true, while the elements.json state reads disabled. F10-029 says inert, so the rebuild should follow that.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory's measured size (title bar 1180x46, tabpanel 1026x715) conflicts with F10-001, which says the Settings window opens at a fixed 640 x 520. The desktop build should be a separate window at the fixed size from F10-001. The recorded size should be checked before it is used as the layout reference.

author: Haiku critic
text: The discard-all control has three different descriptions. The inventory puts an undo clear icon on the Application and Reset SectionHeaders, with a title that says it discards changes since the window opened, and says it may not render. Feature F10-027 places a discard-all (undo) button in the title bar that appears after any change, and F10-034 describes a group header dot that discards changes. Decide one location and one visibility rule for the rebuild, and record the title bar and dot as widgets or remove them from the spec.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory has no clear-search control for the sidebar search field (widget 'InputWell > TextInput2'). Feature F10-011 requires an x button that appears while the query is non-empty, and F10-010 requires a blue focus outline; neither appears as a widget or state. Add the clear button and the focused-outline state to the search field entry, and state that Escape clears the query first (F10-023).

author: Haiku critic
text: The reset job is named four different ways: the row title 'Restore defaults', the button 'Reset all settings…', the confirm button 'Reset everything', and the undo tooltip 'Discard changes made since this window opened'. Pick one verb and noun for the reset control and its confirmation so the rebuilt About pane and the search terms in F10-073 match the visible label.

author: Haiku critic
text: The PathButton entry records only the non-null path and says the null state renders with no path shown, without saying what appears. Feature F10-040 requires a dash while the data folder location is loading, and the inventory has no loading state for this widget. Add the loading and null states, with their exact text, to the PathButton entry.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Data folder SettingRow, the PathButton and the Application description are tied to a local folder. The web app is cloud-based with server-side files, so there is no local data folder to open, and the description 'Tasks, attachments, screenshots and preferences' names screenshots that the web app does not have. Replace or remove the Data folder row, and rewrite the description to describe only the stored data the web app actually holds.

author: Haiku critic
text: The title bar with the three macOS traffic lights (WindowControls, MacLights, the close, minimize and full-screen Light buttons, and the draggable TitleBar) is window chrome that a browser tab does not have. Drop these widgets in the web build and keep only the 'Settings' page heading, which is the Label h1. The desktop build keeps the chrome, with its inert minimize and full-screen lights as recorded.

author: Haiku critic
text: The keyboard behaviour in feature F10-024 and F10-025 conflicts with the web rebuild. Escape closing the Settings window has no meaning in a browser page, and Command-F or Ctrl-F focusing the sidebar search would override the browser's own find shortcut, which the web build must not do. Remove these bindings from the web version and keep the search field reachable by normal focus.

author: Haiku critic
text: The window size conflicts between the sources. Feature F10-001 says the Settings window opens at a fixed 640 x 520 size, but the inventory's frame and title bar were measured at 1180 x 760 from the reference screenshot. Confirm the intended fixed size before the desktop build, and record it in the Settings window frame region, because the content pane and sidebar positions depend on it.

author: Haiku critic
text: The footer-right screenshot ToolbarButton, its screenshot_monitor icon, the Capturing Spinner, the screenshot HotkeyHint and the Cmd+Shift+Enter key action all depend on screen capture, which the web version does not have. Remove them, and decide what replaces the footer-right slot (the web app uploads files to the server, so a file attach control is one option, but the inventory does not establish that). Otherwise the slot has no purpose in the web build.

author: Haiku critic
text: The inventory shows no widget for the global summon/dismiss hotkey, the click-away dismiss, or the tray entry points, yet the features list (F14-001, F14-024, F14-040 to F14-042) depends on them. The desktop rebuild needs a place in the spec for these entry points, or an explicit note that they live outside this screen.

author: Haiku critic
text: Cmd+Enter does different things depending on focus. In the notes editor it submits (submitOnModEnter), while the global capture-enter feature dismisses when the title is focused (F13-016), and plain Enter in the title saves. Pick one submit model for the same job, and state the outcome of each path in the spec.

author: Haiku critic
text: Submitting has no visible outcome in the inventory. Features F13-015 and F14-046 say submit creates the task, clears the draft and dismisses the bar, and the spec has no widget or state for success or failure feedback. Add an explicit post-submit state for both builds, since the web build has no window to dismiss.

author: Haiku critic
text: The Clear ToolbarButton, the target button and the screenshot button all carry tabIndex -1, so keyboard users cannot reach them with Tab (F13-041), and the collapsed Tab-hint button has no focus style. The web build should make these controls tabbable with a visible focus ring, since browser shortcuts take precedence and keyboard reachability is required.

author: Haiku critic
text: Two ToolbarButtons with the same size xs, well variant use different icon sizes (Clear uses iconSize 16, the screenshot button uses iconSize 15) for no stated reason. The collapsed Tab-hint button also has no hover state while the other footer and title buttons change text colour on hover. Pick one icon size and one hover rule for all ToolbarButtons.

author: Haiku critic
text: The formatting tooltips show ⌘B, ⌘I and ⌘U, and the Clear tooltip shows ⌘⇧⌫. Because browser shortcuts take precedence in the web build, Cmd+B, Cmd+I and Cmd+U may be taken by the browser, so these hints may be wrong there. The web build needs a shortcut mapping check, and the hint text should follow the shortcut that actually works.

author: Haiku critic
text: The bar is a frameless window whose height changes from 116 px to 185 px when the notes open, and it is anchored to the cursor edge (F14-015 to F14-019). The desktop build should resize a separate window and keep its anchor and screen-edge flip logic, which the inventory only describes as card heights. The web build needs none of this, since the capture bar is desktop-only.
